Special package for development of J&K 
   2. SHRI T.S. BAJWA: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be to state: 
(i) whether Government have announced any special package for ) 
moment of Jammu and Kashmir; 
(ii) if so, the details thereof; and 
:) the amount spent on different sectors during the year 2002-03? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS ( 
SHRI HARIN PATHAK): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the table of the 
Statement 
(a) and (b) The Prime Minister during his visit to Jammu & Kashmir 8.5.2002 
had announced a package for "employment, rail and road lmopment, relief & 
Security" for J&K to be implemented over a period to 10 years. The main 
development related schemes/projects red in the package comprise 
railways, roads, development of es, Agri-export zones for apples and 
walnuts, development of culture, eco-restoration of degraded catchment areas 
of Chenab and in, Border Area Development Programme etc. 

RAJYA SABHA [9 April, 2003] 
In addition, Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion have in June, 
2002 notified a "New Industrial Policy and other concessions for the State of 
J&K" which comprises incentives like capital investment subsidy, interest 
subsidy, insurance premium, income tax exemption etc. 
(c) The above mentioned schemes and projects are being implemented by 
various concerned Ministries/Departments. As informed by the concerned 
Ministries/Deptts., a sum of approximately Rs. 346.75 crore have been released 
so far during the year 2002-03 towards implementation of the package which 
includes Rs. 236.45 crore for Railways, Rs. 4.06 crores for roads, Rs. 2.9 
crores for development of traditional cottage industries, Rs. 100 crores for 
Border Area Development Programme and Rs. 3.32 crores for eco-restoration of 
degraded catchments of Chenab, Jhelum and Shivaliks.

RAJYA SABHA [9 April, 2003] 
Threatening of terrorist strikes by terrorist outfit 
*383. SHRIMATI SAVITA SHARDA:  Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether terrorist outfit 'Lashkar-e -Taiba' has threatened to carry 
out a fresh series of terrorist strikes on a large scale in India; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the steps Government have taken to meet the threat? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI HARIN PATHAK): (a) to (c) A stat ement is laid on the Table of the 
House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) 'Lashkar-e-Toiba' and other Pak Islamic groups such as Jaish-e-
Mohammad have been targeting individuals, installations and institutions in 
Jammu and Kashmir and have extended their activities to the Indian hinterland 
in recent years. 
(c) In order to tackle the menace of terrorism, the Central Government has 
adopted a multi-pronged approach which includes strengthening of the borders, 
galvanizing the intelligence machinery, monitoring of well coordinated 
intelligence based operations, modernization of State Police Forces and CPMFs 
and strengthening of international/bilateral cooperation to counter cross border 
crime and terrorism. 
The Central Government has been sensitizing the State Governments from 
time to time about the threat perception generated due to terrorist groups 
activities.

*388. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY : Will the Minister of POWER be 
pleased to state what are the steps Gove rnment have taken to ensure adequate 
power supply in Delhi and to narrow the gap between the demand and the 
supply of power in the coming months in the Capital? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI ANANT GANGARAM GEETE): A 
Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
Supply and distribution of power in Delhi is in the purview of 
Government of NCT of Delhi. However, electricity being a concurrent 
subject, Ministry of Power, Government of India reviews power supply 
position in the National Capital, Delhi from time to time and provides 
assistance, whenever required, to augmen t availability of power. It has been 
ascertained that as against the anticipated peak demand of 3200 MW in April, 
2003 and 3700 MW in July/August, 2003, the supply of 
24 

[9 April, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
power has been arranged from various sources in the range of 3300 MW-
3800 MW in the different months. (The peak demand registered during the 
summer of 2002 was 3347 MW). 
The following steps have been taken and assistance provided by the 
Government of India to improve the availability of power in Delhi during the 
ensuing summer months: 
1. 197 MW has been allocated from the unallocated quota of Central 
Generating Stations in Northern Re gion to Delhi with effect from 
1st April, 2003. 
2. Allocation of entire 15% unallocat ed quota (66 MW) in Rajasthan 
Atomic Power Project (RAPP-B) Units III & IV has been made 
from mid-April, 2003. 
3. Arrangements have been tied up by National Thermal Power 
Corporation Limited (NTPC) for procuring liquid fuel to make up 
for any shortfall in supply of gas fuel for its gas based power plants 
in the Northern Region of which Delhi is also a beneficiary. 
4. No shut down of generating units in Northern Region has been 
planned by NTPC during May-August, 2003. 
5. Arrangements have been made through Power Trading Corporation 
(PTC) for purchase of 320 to 390 MW from various sources. 
As per information ascertained from Government of NCT Delhi/ Delhi 
Transco Ltd. (DTL), the following steps have been/are being taken to 
augment and ensure reliability of power supply in Delhi. 
1. Commissioning of 400 KV Bamnouli-Ballabgarh double circuit line 
by 30th April, 2003 to complete 400 KV transmission ring around 
Delhi. 
2. Addition of 900 MVA transformation capacity in Delhi system upto 
May, 2003 out of which 400 MVA has already been added. 
3. Arrangements tied up with concerned agencies for procuring liquid 
fuel to make up shortfall in supply of gas to its gas based power 
plants. 
25 

RAJYA SABHA [9 April. 2003] 
4. DTL and Distribution Companies augmenting the availability of 
shunt capacitors in Delhi Power System including rectification of 
defective capacitors so as to improve the voltage profile. 
5. DTL/Distribution Companies to launch campaigns to promote 
energy efficiency and energy conservation measures. 
6. DTL has made arrangements for procuring additional 80-440 MW 
in the different months from Hi machal Pradesh State Electricity 
Board (HPSEB) bilaterally. 
7. DTL to tie up additional 100-150 MW from other States. 
8. Arrangements made to ensure that no planned shut-down is required 
for maintenance of generating units between May to August, 2003.

Fraud prevention comm ittees/task forces have been set up to formulate 
rules to prevent frauds and take proactive fraud control and enforcement 
measures. Banks have been advised to actively participate in such fraud 
prevention committees/task forces. 
Credit Information Bureaux have been set up to provide a mechanism for 
mitigating credit risk by enhancing the quality of credit decisions. The banks 
have been advised to become members of such Credit Information Bureaux in 
order to maintain the selectivity of customers in their credit card business.

PTS for power 
2886. SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD: Will the Minister of POWER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that one of the pre-requisites for any 
Public Transport System (PTS) is the availability of power or fuel; 
(b) if so, whether Government have ample resources to ensure the 
necessary power supply or fuel supply; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHRIMATI 
JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) Electricity is consumed by Railways for traction. 
Apart from motor spirit and High Speed Diesel (HSD), Compressed Natural 
Gas (CNG) and Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG) have also been permitted for 
use in public transport system. 
(b) The electricity consumption of the Indian Railways for traction is only 
2.2% of the country's total consumption.. State Electricity Boards/ Power 
Companies from whom Railways purchas e electricity for traction purposes 
accord highest priority for supplying power. The existing refining capacity of 
116.07 Million Tonnes per annum is more than the estimated current annual 
demand of around 104 Million Tonnes of petroleum products. The import 
dependence in oil sector is of around 69%. 
(c) There is no power cut to public transport system or shortage of 
transporation fuels i.e. petrol, diesel and aviation transport fuel.

Private power projects 
2889. SHRI MURLI DEORA: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased 
to state: 
(a) the total number of private power projects existing at present in the 
country, State-wise; 
(b) the number of these projects sanctioned by Central Electricity 
Authority till date and by when these plants will start generating power in 
addition to (a) above; 
(c) the manner by which the power produced by these private plants will be 
utilized; and 
(d) the assistance provided by Government to these plants, State-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHRIMATI 
JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) A total of 52 private power projects are presently 
existing in the country.The State-wise break-up is Himachal Pradesh-2, Gujarat-9, 
Maharashtra-8, Goa-1, Andhra Pradesh-5, Kerala-3, Karnataka-6, Tamil 
Nadu-5, Jharkhand-1, West Bengal-9, Assam-2 and Andaman & Nicobar-1 
.These also include the power projects of private licensee companies which 
were in existence even prior to announcement of the policy in 1991 to 
encourage greater private sector participation in the power sector. 
(b) Out of a total of 61 private power projects accorded techno-eco-nomic 
clearance (TEC) by the Central Electricity  Authority (CEA), 16 projects have 
so far been commissioned, which are included in the projects mentioned under 
reply to (a) above. Of the remaining 45 projects, 4 are no longer being pursued 
through private sector by the respective States. The commissioning of the 
balance 41 projects depends upon tying up  of the required inputs/clearances 
(including financial closure) by the project developers. 
(c) Power from the private power project s is generally fed into the State 
Grid for further distribution. 
(d) Government of India (Gol) has been facilitating implementation of 
151 

RAJYA  SABHA [9 April, 2003] 
these projects in trying up the required inputs/clearances though no financial 
assistance is being provided for privat e sector power projects. However, Gol 
has provided counter guarantee to 6 out of 8 identified private sector power 
projects viz. the 740 MW Dabhol (Phase-I) and 1082 MW Bhadrawati power 
projects in Maharashtra, 216 MW Jegurupadu (Phase-I) and 1040 MW 
Visakhapatnam projects in Andhra Pradesh, 250 MW Neyveli-Zero Unit project 
in Tamil Nadu and 420 MW lb Valley project (Units 3 & 4) in Orissa with to 
provide financial comfort to the investors and their lenders.Three of the projects 
viz. Dabhol (Phase-I), Jegurupadu (Phase-I) and Neyveli-Zero Unit having a total 
capacity of 1206 MW have been commissioned. Counter guarantees given for 
the Bhadrawati and Visakhapatnam projects have lapsed due to inability of 
the projects to comply with the required conditions. Counter guarantee given 
to the lb Valley project has also, lapsed since the project parameters have been 
changed with the new capacity being 500 MW (Units 5 & 6). 
One of the projects ( viz., Godavari CCGT in Andhra Pradesh) withdrew 
the request for a Gol counter guarantee. Counter guarantee could not be issued 
to the Mangalore project in Karnatak a since the State Government did not 
accept the prescribed conditions.

the European Union and Canada had been governed by bilateral textile agreements 
entered into between India and these countries under the aegis of the Multi-Fibre 
Arrangement (MFA), outside the rules of the General Agreement on Tariffs 
and Trade (GATT). With effect from January 1,190S. the quantitative 
restrictions (import quotas) in the bilateral agreements under the MFA, are being 
governed by the Agreement on Textiles and Clothing (ATC) contained in the 
Final Act of the Uruguay Round nego tiations of the GATT. Presently, our 
textiles and clothing exports f ace restraints in U.S.A., European Union and 
Canada. 
One of the central elements of the Agreement on Textiles and Clothing (ATC) 
is the four-stage process for the progressive integration of textiles and clothing 
products as specified in the Annex to the ATC into GATT 1994 over a ten-year 
transition period. The integration process has however not led to any meaningful 
removal of quotas by the restraining countries so far. India has raised the issue of 
lack of progressive liberalization in international trade in textilec bilaterally and 
also at the World Trade Organization. In accordance with ATC, all the textile 
quotas would be phased out and textile sector fully integrated into WTO by 1st 
January 2005.

BASANGOUDA R. PATH): (a) to (c) With respect to anti-dumping practices, 
the Ministerial Conference in Doha had mandated negotiations aimed at clarifying 
and improving disciplines under the Anti-dumping Agreement while 
preserving the basic concepts, principa ls and effectiveness of the Agreement 
and its instruments and objectives, and taking into consideration the needs of 
developing and least-developed participants. In the initial phase of the

emphasized in this connection that the Ministerial mandate specifically 
requires that "the needs of developing and least-developed 
participants" be taken into account.

dumping—initiations—as a matter for improved discipline.

Subsidies and Countervailing Measures are being undertaken in the Negotiating 
Group on Rules (NG Rules). Five meetings of the NG Rules have so far been 
held and three more meetings are scheduled prior to the Cancum Ministerial

Rehabilitation of Camp Inmates of kokrajhar District In Assam 
(SHRI URKHAO GWARA BRAHMA (Assam): Madam, my Special mention 
is regarding rehabilitation of  about 36,000 people, who were affected by the 
ethnic clash of 1996 and 1998, and are staying in the relief camps of Kokrajhar 
district of Assam. Even after a lapse of six long years also, the poor inmates 
have not been rehabilitated properly. The greatest problem faced by them is lack 
of funds. The Central Government reimburses the money only after the State 
Government has spent the required amount. The estimated expenditure is about 
Rs. 37,000 crores, and the State Government is passing through a serious 
financial crunch. Unless the Central Government provides the required amount of 
money, the total rehabilitation of these people is not possible. At present, the 
Centre provides money on the reimburs ement basis, and it is clubbed with 
security-related expenditure. There is a delay in the process of reimbursement 
also. On the other hand, till date, the State Government has been able to 
provide only Rs. 2.00 crores. So, in this situation, on humanitarian grounds, the 
Centre should sanction the required amount as one-time grant to accelerate 
the rehabilitation process. At the same time, to help the rehabilitation process, 
the Centre is also requested to sanc tion as many as 33,000 houses under 
Indira Awas Yojana so that poor people staying in relief camps can carry on 
normal life in their respective places. In the case of the cyclone affected people 
of Orissa, the Government of India took some initiative. The case of the riot-
affected people of Kokrajhar district of Assam also should be considered as a 
special case; and this act of kindness may help the district administration to 
complete the process within the short period.

SHRI N.K. PREMACHANDRAN (Kerala): Madam, in the State of Kerala, there are 
2224 unconnected habitations having more than 1000 population and 2306 
unconnected habitations, having more than 500 population. The total number of 
unconnected habitations in the State is 4530. About 45 per cent of all the 
habitations having 500 plus population require connectivity. The need for surfaced 
road in Kerala is around 80,000 kms., showing a shortfall of more than 39,000 kms.

hitherto unconnected rural settlements composed of desom, karas and sub-
desoms. In financial terms, this works out to Rs. 390 crores.

will be around Rs. 300 crores for a year. This means that the due share of Kerala 
State under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, out of the total funds, should be 
Rs. 150 crores.

anguish and concern over the ongoing American and British naked aggression on

from more than hundred countries, the U.S.A. and U.K. have decided unilaterally 
to invade a sovereign country like Iraq under the pretext to change the Saddam 
Hussein regime. And the reason that has been given is that Iraq possesses 
Weapons of Mass Destruction, inspite of the United Nations' inspectors making a 
statement that no such weapons could be found, the allies led by the United 
States have indulged in this sort of advent urism. Sir, in this span of 50 years, I 
was always dreaming* that we should not be threatened with the return of the world 
order where the mightly could subjugate the weak and prey on them. We have 
been at the receiving end for centur ies together. Lodhis, Khiljis, Sayyads,

Portuguese, the Dutch and the East India Company, all foreigners rules this

maintianing sovereignty over this country. And, we had lost renaissance; we had 
lost two great industrial revolutions. And we should have known the value of the 
country's sovereignty, individual freedom. What I am trying to say is, we should 
have reacted long time back. That is why I say, it is like bolting the stables after

satisfaction that, notwithstanding the avoi dable delay, the fact that the hon.

Members of this House will recall, some of us had raised the need for adoption

was an understanding among a section of the House that a doption of such a 
Resolution will inhibit the diplomatic la titude, the diplomatic elbow-room that

Indian Parliament to express itself in very unambiguous terms because the 
problem is, the Iraq developments have shown failure of global diplomacy. Had the 
sequence of evidence underscored the need for greater diplomatic

SHRI RG. NARAYANAN (Tamil Nadu): Madam Deputy Chairperson, I rise to 
support the Resolution on Iraq. On behalf of the All India Anna DMK, I express 
my regrets and anguish on the war waged by the United States and the U.K. on 
Iraq, inspite of the opposition by majority of the nations in the world, and, also, 
in violation of the advice given by the United Nations. It is a matter of great 
regret that,-in this war, innocent people are being killed. On behalf of my Party, 
I strongly condemn the unilateral decision of the United States, supported by a 
few nations like the United Kingdom, to enf orce war on Iraq, without any basic 
reason and in utter disregard of the world opinion. I appeal to the Government to 
take appropriate action to stop the unju stified war on Iraq forthwith, and to 
bring international pressure on America and its allied in order to bring peace in 
the world and to render justice. I also  appeal to the Government to mobilise 
opinion of like-minded nations and bring this unjustifiable war waged by America 
and its allied to immediate halt, and make them quit Iraq with their forces and 
weapons at once, through the intervention of the United Nations.T hank you, 
Madam.

citizens of Iraq. Thousands of people are running for shelter here and there.

Madam, I would like to say that not only Indians are having the feelings against 
America, but even American people are also having the same feeling that 
America should not have waged war against Iraq. Even though we are not having 
any print media, but the electronic medi a and the websites have clearly shown 
that the people of America are not interested in war as it is. The women's groups, 
religious leaders including the Nobel Prize winners have marched on the streets, 
raising slogans against war. A large number of journalists, intellectuals, NGOs 
are also marching on the streets of America saying that there should not be any 
war. Even the political parties of America opposed the war. It was said by one 
of the Members of the American Senate t hat it is a political arrogance of the 
America in waging a war against Iraq, and he said, "Today, I wept, with tears 
rolling down." Another Senator, Edward Kennedy said, "We will certainly win the 
war, but how do we win the peace?" So, even the American people themselves are 
condemning and deploring the actions of America. Our Poet Bharati Dasan said, I 
quote: "If the world waged a war against  humanity, we will destroy the world

invading Iraq and saying, "We want peace and prosperity in Iraq". After the 
destruction of so many houses, so many buildings and so many things, is there 
any possibility of

has also left out some very important issues, I support this Resolution because

at the eleventh hour. In fact, we have discussed this issue in the two all-party 
meetings held by the Prime Minister-before the war was started and after the 
war had started-and also in this House. In these meetings, proposals were 
made that we s hould pass a Resolution. Before the war was started, we

no country shall resort to a war to solve this problem. Otherwise that it should

the Government evaded moving such a Resolution. In fact, they were opposed 
to it. The second time also, in the all-party meeting, the same proposal was 
made. It was disagreed there also. Again when this matter was discussed in this 
House also, they disagreed. Even regarding this Resolution, for the last three 
days a joint discussion was going on as to what should be the text, whether the 
Resolution should be adopted or not. It was mainly because of the stand taken 
by the Government. In fact, now a Resolution has come out, mainly because of 
the fact that the Opposition parties-even though they were holding certain very 
definite views-have attempted and compromised in bringing about a common 
Resolution. It is not that it was brought by the Government on its own. 
The main issue, Madam, was that Iraq was possessing Weapons of Mass 
Destruction. The United Nations Inspection Team have been inspecting for 
years together and a lot of armaments were destroyed. Thereafter, again, the 
Inspection Team was allowed to inspect the places where it suspected that the 
armaments were kept. Six hundred such places were inspected by it. It did not 
find any atomic weapons or nuclear weapons or biological weapons or chemical 
weapons. That may be their suspicion. In that case, the Inspection Team should 
have been allowed to carry on with its inspection for some more time and find 
out whether there are any Weapons of Mass Destruction. Instead of doing 
that, the United States, along with some of their allies, had started a war. They 
unilaterally decided it. It was not decided in the Security council of the United 
Nations. In fact, majority of the Security Council Members were against 
waging a war on Iraq. The United States did it by bypassing or ignoring or 
undermining the United Nations. Apart from that, they also made the United 
Nations ineffective not only for the time-being but also for the future. 
Now I come to the post-war issues. Why did the United States start such a 
high-handed action unilaterally? It is quite clear. I don't want to go into the 
details due to want of time. It has already become clear that they are out to 
establish their hegemony all over the world and they are out to establish a 
world order where they will be in control of the oil
